_step_sweep_meaning: Each row moves the latent along the gradient by that fraction of the latent's own norm, decodes it and scores it. A rising log p(target) means the gradient points somewhere the classifier likes; it does not mean the panel closed. A NaN row means the decode overflowed at that magnitude, which bounds the step a guided loop may take, and is a property of the step size rather than of the gradient.

gate._meaning: All three must hold before a guided generation is worth its allocation. A finite, non-zero gradient says the path from latent to classifier carries a derivative; it says nothing about whether following it closes a panel.
